title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Elements Zero
summary: Given a 2D array queries, where each query defines an array of integers ranging from l to r.
statement: Given a 2D array queries, where each query defines an array of integers ranging from l to r. An operation consists of selecting two integers from the array and replacing them with their floor division by 4. The goal is to find the minimum number of operations needed to reduce all elements to zero for each query, then sum these results.
constraints: Each query represents the array of every integer from left through right, inclusive.
One operation chooses two current elements and replaces each by floor(value/4).
Return the sum, over all queries, of the minimum operations needed to make every element zero.
hints: Each value contributes its number of repeated divide-by-four steps; an operation performs at most two steps on distinct elements.
Count total steps over a range by power-of-four bands and also obtain the largest individual step count.
Use a cumulative band function for [1,x]; for [l,r], take max(ceil(total/2),steps(r)) and sum queries.
Pairing available steps achieves the total-work bound until only the longest element remains, making the maximum of the two bounds exact.
editorial: Pairing available steps achieves the total-work bound until only the longest element remains, making the maximum of the two bounds exact.

tests.explanation: The two query arrays require one and two operations, totaling three.
The sole value needs three divisions and can be selected only once per operation, so the answer is three.
